test_case_steps: Start an EST server and proxy, configure HTTP Basic authentication, and issue /simpleenroll requests through the proxy using RSA-2048, EC-256, and DSA CSRs. Exercise corrupted CSR, manual-approval/Retry-After, and proof-of-possession enabled/disabled cases.
expected_behavior: Valid CSRs and valid credentials are enrolled successfully; malformed PKCS#10 requests are rejected; manual enrollment returns HTTP 202 with Retry-After; proof-of-possession is accepted or rejected according to the configured policy.

test_case_steps: Start the EST server and proxy and submit /simplereenroll requests for an existing or expired certificate. Exercise preservation of X.509 extensions and public key, corrupted CSR input, manual approval, proof-of-possession/RA certificate combinations, and invalid proxy credentials.
expected_behavior: Valid re-enrollment succeeds and preserves required certificate data; corrupted requests and invalid credentials fail; manual approval produces Retry-After behavior; proof-of-possession and RA authorization rules are enforced.

test_case_steps: Run an EST proxy in front of the server and request /cacerts. Exercise Basic and Digest authentication sanity cases, supported and unsupported TLS versions, valid, revoked, self-signed, explicit and implicit certificate chains, invalid initialization parameters, and use of POST instead of GET.
expected_behavior: A valid /cacerts GET returns HTTP 200 and the configured CA certificate chain. TLS 1.1/1.2 and valid trust chains are accepted; SSL 3.0/TLS 1.0, revoked or untrusted certificates, invalid parameters, invalid credentials, and the wrong HTTP method are rejected.

test_case_steps: Configure CSR attributes on the EST server/proxy through static data and callback variants, then retrieve them through the proxy. Exercise no-data responses, valid and invalid Base64/ASN.1 payloads, size boundaries, callback precedence, and proof-of-possession attribute insertion.
expected_behavior: Valid CSR-attribute data is returned and forwarded correctly; no configured data produces the expected empty/204 behavior; malformed or invalid-size data is rejected; callback data takes precedence where configured; proof-of-possession attributes are added only when required.

test_case_title: Client CSR-attributes retrieval and parsing (native us896.c)
test_case_steps: Initialize an EST client and server, configure the server with CSR-attribute responses, call the client CSR-attributes API, and exercise valid, empty, malformed, corrupted, and boundary-sized responses.
expected_behavior: The client successfully retrieves and parses valid /csrattrs responses and reports the returned data; malformed, corrupt, or invalid inputs are detected and rejected without corrupting the client state.

test_case_title: Client CA-certificate retrieval and validation (native us897.c)
test_case_steps: Initialize clients with different trust-anchor configurations, configure the EST server, issue /cacerts requests, and validate returned certificate material. Exercise single and multi-certificate chains, missing or expired intermediates, responses containing CRLs, invalid server parameters, and read-timeout boundaries.
expected_behavior: Valid CA certificate responses are retrieved and validated successfully; valid chains are accepted, while incomplete or invalid chains and invalid client/server parameters are rejected according to the API and certificate-validation rules.

test_case_steps: Perform an initial enrollment to obtain a certificate, then call the client re-enrollment API using existing and expired certificates. Exercise preservation of X.509 extensions/public key, null certificate/key parameters, corrupted certificates, manual approval with Retry-After, and Basic/Digest authentication success and failure.
expected_behavior: A valid certificate is renewed or rekeyed successfully and required certificate properties are preserved; invalid inputs and credentials fail cleanly; manual approval is surfaced through Retry-After handling.

test_case_steps: Perform /simpleenroll using username/password authentication with both library-generated and application-provided CSRs. Exercise null and corrupt CSR input, server hostname/IP matching through CN and SubjectAltName including wildcard cases, CRL checking, and Retry-After responses.
expected_behavior: Valid enrollment returns a certificate; null or malformed CSRs are rejected; server identity and CRL validation accept matching trusted certificates and reject mismatches or revoked certificates; Retry-After information is available when enrollment is pending.

test_case_steps: Initialize server-side CSR attributes and request them from a client. Exercise null, zero-length, oversized, malformed Base64, valid Base64/ASN.1, boundary-sized values, callback/static configuration, and proof-of-possession augmentation.
expected_behavior: The server accepts valid CSR-attribute configuration and returns correctly encoded attributes; invalid configuration is rejected; empty configuration produces the expected no-data response; proof-of-possession data is included only when enabled.

test_case_title: Server CA-certificate distribution and TLS checks (native us901.c)
test_case_steps: Start the EST server and issue /cacerts requests while exercising Basic/Digest authentication sanity tests, TLS protocol versions, explicit and implicit client certificates, revoked and self-signed certificates, anonymous ciphers, invalid server initialization data, and an invalid POST request to /cacerts.
expected_behavior: A valid GET /cacerts returns HTTP 200 and the CA chain; supported TLS versions and trusted certificates work; obsolete TLS, anonymous ciphers, revoked/untrusted certificates, invalid credentials/initialization, and the wrong HTTP method fail.

test_case_title: Server simple enrollment and PoP validation (native us903.c)
test_case_steps: Start an EST server and submit /simpleenroll requests using RSA, EC, and DSA CSRs. Exercise corrupted PKCS#10, manual enrollment, missing/valid/invalid proof-of-possession, a non-default ECDHE curve, and an RA certificate carrying the appropriate CMC RA usage.
expected_behavior: Valid CSRs enroll successfully; corrupted requests are rejected; manual enrollment returns Retry-After; proof-of-possession is enforced when required and valid RA behavior is handled according to policy.

test_case_steps: Run the high-level provisioning flow that performs /cacerts, /csrattrs, and /simpleenroll. Exercise HTTP Basic authentication with and without a client certificate, authentication-hint variants, null API parameters, and combinations of server PoP and CSR-attribute configuration.
expected_behavior: A correctly configured client completes the full trusted provisioning sequence and receives the CA certificates and enrolled certificate; invalid API parameters fail safely; PoP and CSR-attribute behavior follows server configuration.

test_case_title: TLS-SRP authentication in server and proxy modes (native us1060.c)
test_case_steps: Configure server/proxy authentication combinations from the suite matrix and perform simple enrollment using TLS-SRP. Exercise valid and invalid SRP passwords, HTTP authentication enabled/disabled, and proxy-to-server configurations where SRP is or is not used.
expected_behavior: Valid SRP credentials establish the expected authenticated enrollment path; invalid SRP or HTTP credentials fail; configurations that intentionally disable HTTP authentication continue to work with valid SRP; unsupported combinations are rejected.

test_case_steps: Configure the server with required CSR attributes and perform simple enrollment with CSRs that contain all required attributes, omit required values, use an incorrect EC curve or digest, contain large/extra attributes, and run with proof-of-possession enabled and disabled.
expected_behavior: Enrollment succeeds when the CSR satisfies the configured CA requirements and fails when required attributes, key parameters, or digest constraints are violated; permitted extra attributes are handled without breaking valid enrollment.

test_case_steps: Exercise the server authentication-mode API, perform a Basic-authentication sanity enrollment, switch the server to token authentication, and issue an unauthenticated request while inspecting the returned HTTP authentication challenge.
expected_behavior: Valid authentication-mode configuration is accepted, invalid mode parameters are rejected, Basic mode continues to work before the switch, and token mode returns the expected token/Bearer authentication challenge instead of silently accepting an unauthenticated request.

test_case_steps: Register client credential callbacks and perform enrollment/re-enrollment under token, Basic, and Digest authentication. Exercise missing callback, empty credentials, valid token, wrong token, oversized token, forced callback error, and valid Basic/Digest credential callbacks.
expected_behavior: A valid token or valid Basic/Digest credentials result in successful authentication and certificate issuance; missing, empty, incorrect, oversized, or callback-error credentials fail; the correct credential callback is invoked for the server challenge.

test_case_title: Proxy authentication modes for enroll and re-enroll (native us2174.c)
test_case_steps: Start an EST server and proxy and perform simple enrollment and re-enrollment while varying proxy and upstream server authentication between Basic and token modes. Supply the corresponding credential callbacks and accepted tokens for each configuration.
expected_behavior: Supported proxy/server authentication combinations propagate credentials correctly and allow valid enrollment or re-enrollment; invalid or mismatched authentication credentials are rejected and the configured callbacks are exercised.

test_case_title: Client URI path-segment extension validation (native us3496.c)
test_case_steps: Configure the EST client server URI with no path segment and with multiple candidate path segments. Exercise a valid single segment, all permitted characters, multiple segments, invalid characters, empty value, oversized value, colon-containing value, and values equal to or containing EST operation names.
expected_behavior: Valid single path segments are accepted and incorporated into the EST URI; malformed, empty, multi-segment, or oversized values are rejected according to the path-segment validation rules, while permitted characters are preserved.

test_case_title: Server and proxy URI path-segment propagation (native us3512.c)
test_case_steps: Exercise simple enrollment, re-enrollment, /cacerts, and /csrattrs with configured URI path segments in direct server and proxy modes. Test valid, maximum-length, oversized, reserved-operation, and operation-containing segments and inspect values passed to server/proxy callbacks.
expected_behavior: Valid path segments are parsed and propagated to the appropriate operation and authentication callbacks in both direct and proxy modes; invalid or oversized segments are rejected without misrouting the EST operation.

test_case_steps: Load a password-protected private key using the correct and incorrect passphrases and attempt simple enrollment. Change the password callback after a key has already been loaded, and exercise RSA/EC key-generation utilities with and without password protection.
expected_behavior: A correctly decrypted private key can be used for enrollment; an incorrect password prevents key loading/enrollment; changing the later callback does not corrupt an already loaded key; generated RSA/EC keys follow the requested protection behavior.

test_case_title: Client HTTP and SOCKS proxy modes (native us4020.c)
test_case_steps: Exercise the client proxy-configuration API with invalid parameters and valid SOCKS4, SOCKS4A, SOCKS5, and HTTP proxy configurations. Perform certificate enrollment through the configured proxy with no credentials, valid credentials, missing credentials, and invalid credentials as applicable.
expected_behavior: Valid proxy configurations route EST enrollment successfully; supported credential combinations authenticate as expected; malformed API parameters, unsupported modes, and invalid proxy credentials are rejected cleanly.
